title: Text 3
subtitle: 维多利亚人的微笑与拍照

sentences.en: As a historian who’s always searching for the text or the image that makes us re- evaluate the past, I’ve become preoccupied with looking for photographs that show our Victorian ancestors smiling (what better way to shatter the image of 19th-century prudery?).
sentences.zh: 作为一名一直致力于寻找能让我们重新评价过去的文本或图像的历史学家，我痴迷于寻找能展现维多利亚时代祖先微笑的照片（还有什么比这更能粉碎19世纪假正经的形象呢？）。

sentences.en: I’ve found quite a few, and — since I started posting them on Twitter — they have been causing quite a stir.
sentences.zh: 我已经找到了不少这样的照片，而且——自从我开始把它们发到Twitter上以来——它们引起了不小的轰动。

sentences.en: People have been surprised to see evidence that Victorians had fun and could, and did, laugh.
sentences.zh: 人们惊讶地发现，有证据表明维多利亚时代的人也会寻欢作乐，能够欢笑，而且确实笑了。

sentences.en: They are noting that the Victorians suddenly seem to become more human as the hundred-or-so years that separate us fade away through our common experience of laughter.
sentences.zh: 他们注意到，随着把我们隔开的百年左右的时光在共同的欢笑体验中消融，维多利亚时代的人似乎突然变得更加有人情味了。

sentences.en: Of course, I need to concede that my collection of “Smiling Victorians” makes up only a tiny percentage of the vast catalogue of photographic portraiture created between 1840 and 1900, the majority of which show sitters posing miserably and stiffly in front of painted backdrops, or staring absently into the middle distance.
sentences.zh: 当然，我必须承认，我收集的“微笑的维多利亚人”只占1840年至1900年间拍摄的海量摄影肖像中的极小一部分，其中大多数照片里的被摄者要么在绘制的背景前痛苦而僵硬地摆着姿势，要么茫然地盯着中景发呆。

sentences.en: How do we explain this trend?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何解释这一趋势呢？

sentences.en: During the 1840s and 1850s, in the early days of photography, exposure times were notoriously long: the daguerreotype photographic method (producing an image on a silvered copper plate) could take several minutes to complete, resulting in blurred images as sitters shifted position or adjusted their limbs.
sentences.zh: 在19世纪40年代和50年代，摄影术尚处于早期，曝光时间以漫长而著称：达盖尔银版摄影法（在镀银铜板上成像）可能需要几分钟才能完成，由于被摄者移动位置或调整肢体，结果导致图像模糊。

sentences.en: The thought of holding a fixed grin as the camera performed its magical duties was too much to contemplate, and so a non- committal blank stare became the norm.
sentences.zh: 一想到要在相机执行其神奇任务时保持固定的咧嘴笑容，实在令人难以忍受，于是面无表情的呆滞凝视便成了常态。

sentences.en: But exposure times were much quicker by the 1880s, and the introduction of the Box Brownie and other portable cameras meant that, though slow by today’s digital standards, the exposure was almost instantaneous.
sentences.zh: 但到19世纪80年代，曝光时间已经快得多，布朗尼盒式相机等便携式相机的问世意味着，虽然以今天的数码标准来看速度仍显缓慢，但曝光几乎是瞬间完成的。

sentences.en: Spontaneous smiles were relatively easy to capture by the 1890s, so we must look elsewhere for an explanation of why Victorians still hesitated to smile.
sentences.zh: 到19世纪90年代，捕捉自然流露的微笑已相对容易，因此，要解释维多利亚时代的人为何仍不愿微笑，我们只能另寻原因。

sentences.en: One explanation might be the loss of dignity displayed through a cheesy grin.
sentences.zh: 一种解释可能是，露齿傻笑会显得有失尊严。

sentences.en: “Nature gave us lips to conceal our teeth,” ran one popular Victorian saying, alluding to the fact that before the birth of proper dentistry, mouths were often in a shocking state of hygiene.
sentences.zh: “大自然赐予我们嘴唇来遮蔽牙齿。”一句维多利亚时代的流行谚语这样说道，它暗指这样一个事实：在现代牙科诞生之前，人们的口腔常常处于令人震惊的卫生状况。

sentences.en: A flashing set of healthy and clean, regular “pearly whites” was a rare sight in Victorian society, the preserve of the super-rich (and even then, dental hygiene was not guaranteed).
sentences.zh: 在维多利亚时代的社会里，一口健康、清洁、整齐的“珍珠白”牙齿十分罕见，那是超级富豪的专属（即便如此，也未必能保证口腔卫生）。

sentences.en: A toothy grin (especially when there were gaps or blackened teeth) lacked class: drunks, tramps, and music hall performers might gurn and grin with a smile as wide as Lewis Carroll’s gum-exposing Cheshire Cat, but it was not a becoming look for properly bred persons.
sentences.zh: 龇牙咧嘴的笑（尤其当牙齿有豁口或发黑时）显得很没档次：醉汉、流浪汉和音乐厅演员或许会做出鬼脸，咧嘴笑到像刘易斯·卡罗尔笔下咧嘴露牙龈的柴郡猫一样大，但对教养良好的人来说，这可不是体面的样子。

sentences.en: Even Mark Twain, a man who enjoyed a hearty laugh, said that when it came to photographic portraits there could be “nothing more damning than a silly, foolish smile fixed forever”.
sentences.zh: 就连喜欢开怀大笑的马克·吐温都说，谈及摄影肖像，没有比“一个愚蠢的、傻乎乎的笑容被永远定格”更糟糕的了。

questions.stem: What does the author say about the Victorian portraits he has collected?

options.A: They are in popular use among historians.
options.B: They are rare among photographs of that age.
options.D: They show effects of different exposure times.

questions.analysis: 本题为细节题。根据题干关键词the Victorian portraits he has collected定位到第二段①句中的my collection of ‘Smiling Victorians’ makes up only a tiny percentage of the vast catalogue of photographic portraiture created between 1840 and 1900。They are rare among photographs of that age是对makes up only a tiny percentage of the vast catalogue of photographic portraiture created between 1840 and 1900的概括总结。所以本题选B。

questions.stem: What might have kept the Victorians from smiling for pictures in the 1890s?
questions.analysis: 本题为细节题。根据题干关键词kept the Victorians from smiling for pictures in the 1890s定位到第四段②句Spontaneous smiles were relatively easy to capture by the 1890s, so we must look elsewhere for an explanation of why Victorians still hesitated to smile。该句指出在19世纪90年代，自然的微笑相对容易捕捉，因此需要寻找其他的原因。紧接着第五段作出另一种可能的解释，其中第五段②句中的before the birth of proper dentistry, mouths were often in a shocking state of hygiene说明了口腔卫生状况常常令人震惊，导致维多利亚人拍照时不露齿笑，对应了Their unhealthy dental condition。所以本题选D。

questions.stem: Mark Twain is quoted to show that the disapproval of smiles in pictures was ____
questions.analysis: 本题为例证题。根据题干关键词Mark Twain定位到第六段②句，该句引用了Mark Twain的具体话语。再向前寻找他所要证明的观点，从而定位到第六段①句A toothy grin (especially when there were gaps or blackened teeth) lacked class，即“露齿微笑缺少修养”，这是一种根深蒂固的观念，对应A项a deep-root belief。所以本题选A。

questions.stem: Which of the following questions does the text answer?

options.A: Why did most Victorians look stern in photographs?
options.B: When did the Victorians start to view photography differently?
options.C: What made photography develop slowly in the Victorian period?
options.D: How did smiling in photographs become a post-Victorian norm?

questions.analysis: 本题为主旨大意题。全文前两段提出维多利亚时代人们拍照时普遍不会微笑这一现象，接下来第三段至第六段分别从曝光时间，牙齿健康状况以及固有观念这三方面分析现象背后的原因，因此A项Why did most Victorians look stern in photographs?是对原文主旨的概括。所以本题选A。
